The difference between a specific field course and a general history course that covers multiple art periods as in the case of FA 171; the later requires the instructor to have knowledge about not only the specific paintings and sculptures covered within the class but also requires knowledge about the history of the period regardless from the art (such as political, literature, music and theatre, etc). Instructor was lacking the necessary knowledge about western political and social history as well as knowledge about the history of literature and other applied arts which in my opinion has great importance in this course. 

Often my question about the reflections and connections of the movements and aesthetics covered within the class with other fields such as literature, politics and music history was unable to be answered by the instructor. I may understand that given this course is geared towards first year students, the level and coverage would be limited. I would understand if she was giving a specific field course which is not connected with different areas, but history of art and culture is a very general course description. The instructor should know more about literature, politics, philosophy and other principles in art field to be able to give this course. 

For example the "Liberty Leading the People" painting by Delacroix a very important and famous work in not only art history but political, literature, philosophy and musical history too. This painting is the single most explicits example of the Nopoleonic wars which showcases the ideals of romantic period as compared to classical period within literature and music. Politically, it showcase the war between republic and monarchy. 

The instructor was not knowledgeable enough about these connecting subjects. Above was just an example from many. Just knowing the art side of selected paintings is not enough to give a culture and history course which supposed to lay the foundation of an art major's intellect.
